rv: Well, this was a surprise, a mini-history of the alphabet and the modern fountain pen, told seamlessly and (excuse the expression) fluidly here for the 20 minute time frame. Although the Alphabet is given a bit too brief of a history, the film does show major developments in the forms, and gives a bit of interesting trivia to go along with it. The pen (since, yes, this film is brought to you by a pen company) is given more of the attention here as we see how the modern pen came to be, how it works, and some new advancements in pen technology (A push button ink sucker! Say it isnt so!).…

The storyline in this short cleverly morphs from the development of the alphabet, to the way it is written, to praise for the soon-to-be-obsolete fountain pen. While one maker of fountain pens touts the benefits, all I can think of is how a group's valuable old minutes were destroyed as their hand-written book got soaked with water and the ink washed off the paper. The narrator, happy and smiling, skips over this possibility. The Jam Handy writer slips in a bit of comic relief to keep the audience interested and make the film a little more enjoyable.

I Think We Are Forgetting Someting-

As outdated and corny as this is, I enjoyed this film's reflection of a weird kind of suburban utopia. Not so much a film as it is a very long ad, it reflects the kinds of hopes and aspirations of average post-war Americans, at least according to what the ad agencies of the day thought. Although this film may seem silly to us today, it was probably quite thrilling to get ones first freezer back then as having one represented a tremendous amount of time-saving. And, of course, Saran Wrap was there to lead the way.
Of course this film was extremely idealistic, superficial, and dated- but it was lots of fun to watch! A real charmer.

In this BADLY dated film, Saran Wrap is seen as the solution to ANY problem around the house. Got excessive meat in the freezer? Wrap it up! Got baby clothes? Wrap it up! Need party favors? Saran Wrap is used to make these god awful looking party favors, that of course are the hit of the party. The wife in the film is just so Saran Wrap obsessed it's almost frightening to comprehend what she'd use the wrap for if her domestic situation took a turn for the worse......

Lets see: Saran wrap (used for everything under the sun including shit up diapers); Westinghouse freezer; florist tape; steel wire; a "woody" station wagon; American Tourister luggage. Never mind that by the time the party favors were completed, Kathy was already 11. The kids look puzzled as there were only 6 candles. This henpecked hubby will be gone in no time. The '60's became "divorceville." The scripted events (stacked one on top of another) made me anxious.

GMM-10069: The Bermuda High pressure system sits over the Atlantic during summer. A normal Bermuda High often leads to hurricanes moving up the east coast and out to sea. During summer 2004 and 2005, the Bermuda High expanded to the south and west, which steered hurricanes into the Gulf of Mexico rather than up the east coast or curving out to sea.
